Assumption A2 requires ρ_rp: R → R to be C¹, but z^{2/p} does not define such a function. The corollary correctly uses |z|^{2/p}, which is C¹ on R for all p ∈ (0,2).

diagnostic_evidence.quote: By Assumption \ref{as:A2}, we have $\sigmainn'(\widetilde w_i(\t_\star)) = 0$ such that $\widetilde w_i'(\t_\star) = 0$. This clearly contradicts the local uniqueness of the trajectory $\wprod$ since on $(\t_\star-\varepsilon,\t_\star)$ both the original trajectory $\gamma_1(\t) = \widetilde w_i(\t)$ and the constant trajectory $\gamma_2(\t) = \widetilde w_i(\t_\star)$ are solutions

issues.failure_explanation: The reparametrized ODE w̃' = h'(w̃)^{⊙-1} ⊙ g(w̃) is only defined on int(wDomainRP)^N, not on all of R^N, since h'(z̃) = [ρ_rp^{-1}]'(z̃)² is only defined for z̃ in the interior of the reparametrized domain. The claim of continuity on R^N is false. Moreover, the uniqueness argument at the boundary hitting time t_* requires the RHS to be locally Lipschitz at the boundary point. For the polynomial reparametrization with p > 1, h'(z̃)^{-1} = (4/p²)z̃^{2-p} has 2-p < 1, so it is not Lipschitz at z̃ = 0, and the uniqueness-based contradiction fails. Additionally, the proof evaluates ρ_rp'(w̃_i(t_*)) which is a type error: ρ_rp' is defined on D (the original domain), not on D_rp (the reparametrized domain) where w̃_i(t_*) lives.

failure_location.quote: Since the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:with_sigmaout_PreVersion} is a continuous function of $\wprod$ on $\R^\N$ by Assumptions \ref{as:A1}-\ref{as:A3}, it is locally Lipschitz continuous at any point.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the uniqueness-at-boundary argument with a standard comparison argument: since h'(z̃)^{-1} → 0 at the boundary (by A2, ρ_rp' → 0 on ∂D implies [ρ_rp^{-1}]' → ∞, hence h' → ∞ and h'^{-1} → 0), the time integral ∫ h'(s)^{-1} ds diverges at the boundary, so the trajectory cannot reach ∂D_rp in finite time.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of orthant preservation (Theorem vector_IRERM (i)) has a technical gap: the stated local-Lipschitz-on-R^N argument does not go through at the boundary for reparametrizations where h'(z̃)^{-1} is not Lipschitz at ∂D_rp. The conclusion (trajectory stays in the interior) remains correct.
issues.title: Boundary regularity gap in orthant-preservation proof
issues.why_classification: The conclusion is correct and well-established in the literature; the fix is a standard local ODE argument (divergence of the time-to-boundary integral) that replaces the flawed uniqueness step without altering any statement or requiring new architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: all that remains is to show that $h'(\wprod(\t))^{\odot-1} = c_p^{-1} \wprod(\t)^{\odot(2-p)} \ge r$, for some $r > 0$ depending only on $p$ and $\wprod_0$, and all $\t \ge 0$.

For $p \le 1$, this lower bound on $\wprod(\t)$ can be deduced from Lemma \ref{lem:decay} by refining the argument for $\wprodinfty \in \R_{>0}^\N$ appearing in the proof of Corollary \ref{cor:PolynomialRegularizationNonAsymptotic}.

issues.failure_explanation: The linear convergence claim requires h'(w̃(t))^{⊙-1} ≥ r > 0 for all t ≥ 0, which for the polynomial reparametrization (where h'(z̃)^{-1} = (4/p²)z̃^{2-p}) is equivalent to w̃(t) being bounded away from 0 uniformly in time. The proof explicitly defers this step. While the limit-time argument (w̃_∞ ∈ R_{>0}^N) is established in the non-asymptotic corollary, the uniform-in-time lower bound w̃(t) ≥ r^{1/(2-p)} for all t ≥ 0 is a distinct, nontrivial claim that is not proved. The argument from Lemma lem:decay (boundedness of D_F) combined with the divergence of h(z̃) → -∞ as z̃ → 0⁺ (for p ≤ 1) does yield the bound, but this derivation is absent from the source.

failure_location.quote: \johannes{We} leave this refinement to the interested reader.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing argument: from Lemma lem:decay, D_F(z̃_0, w̃(t)) ≤ D_F(z̃_0, w̃(0)) < ∞ for all t. For p ≤ 1, h(w̃_i) = (p²/(4(p-1)))w̃_i^{p-1} → -∞ as w̃_i → 0⁺, so the Bregman term -h(w̃_i)(z̃_{0,i} - w̃_i) → +∞ as w̃_i → 0. Hence w̃_i(t) ≥ δ > 0 for all i, t, where δ depends on z̃_0, w̃(0), and p. This gives h'(w̃(t))^{⊙-1} ≥ (4/p²)δ^{2-p} =: r > 0.
issues.overall_effect: The exponential convergence rate for p ∈ (0,1] under the PL condition is stated as a corollary but lacks a complete proof; the missing uniform positivity estimate is a nontrivial step that the reader is asked to supply.
issues.title: Incomplete proof of linear convergence for polynomial p ∈ (0,1]
issues.why_classification: The missing step is a contained but nontrivial uniform-in-time estimate requiring the interplay between the Bregman divergence bound and the singular behavior of h near 0; it is more than a one-line fix but does not require new proof architecture or change any statement.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume that there exists $\z_0 \in \R^\N$ with $\A\z_0 = \y$ and set $\w_0 = \0$.
the following claims hold for all $\wprod_0 \in \mathrm{int} (\wDomainRP)$

issues.failure_explanation: The intro theorem thm:TrigonometricRegularizationIntroduction sets w_0 = 0, giving w̃_0 = ρ_rp(0) = 0 (for both sinh and tanh). The convergence corollary (i) requires w̃_0 > 0, which excludes w̃_0 = 0. However, the general convergence theorem (thm:Convergence) only requires w̃_0 ∈ int(wDomainRP). For sinh, wDomainRP = R^N and int = R^N, so 0 ∈ int. For tanh, wDomainRP = [-1,1]^N and int = (-1,1)^N, so 0 ∈ int. Thus the general theorem covers w̃_0 = 0, but the corollary as stated does not, creating a gap in the logical chain from the general results to the intro theorem's convergence claim.

failure_location.quote: For any $\wprod_0 > 0$, the trajectory $\wprod(\t) = \sigmainn(\w(\t))$ converges to a limit $\wprodinfty \in \wDomainRP$ with $\LossM (\wprodinfty) = 0$ with the rate characterized in Theorem \ref{thm:Convergence} \ref{thm:Convergence_i}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the hypothesis in cor:TrigonometricRegularizationConvergence (i) from 'For any w̃_0 > 0' to 'For any w̃_0 ∈ int(wDomainRP)'; the proof already works under this more general condition since it invokes Theorem thm:Convergence which requires only w̃_0 ∈ int(wDomainRP).
issues.overall_effect: The intro theorem's claim that the limit exists for w_0 = 0 is not supported by the convergence corollary as stated; the general theorem does cover this case, but the paper's stated logical derivation (intro theorem from corollaries) has a gap.
issues.title: Convergence corollary excludes zero initialization used in intro theorem
issues.why_classification: A one-phrase correction to the hypothesis that aligns the corollary with both the general theorem and the intro theorem's usage; the proof requires no modification and no mathematical content is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\sigmainn \colon \R \to \R$ is continuously differentiable and there exist closed and convex intervals $\wDomainOneD, \wDomainRPOneD \subset \R$ such that $\sigmainn \colon \wDomainOneD \to \wDomainRPOneD$ is invertible with $\sigmainn'(z)=0$ if and only if $z \in \partial \wDomainOneD$.
In both cases $\sigmainn = \sinh$ and $\sigmainn = \tanh$ this is fulfilled since $\sigmainn' \neq 0$ and $\partial \wDomainOneD = \emptyset$.

issues.failure_explanation: Assumption A2 requires ρ_rp: D → D_rp to be invertible (bijective) between closed intervals D and D_rp. For ρ_rp = tanh with D = R, the image is tanh(R) = (-1,1), which is not a closed interval. No closed interval D_rp ⊂ R admits tanh: R → D_rp as a surjection (tanh never attains ±1). The proofs of both cor:TrigonometricRegularizationConvergence and cor:TrigonometricRegularizationNonAsymptotic claim A2 holds for tanh by checking only 'ρ_rp' ≠ 0 and ∂D = ∅', which is necessary but not sufficient; the surjectivity-onto-a-closed-interval requirement is the missing (and failed) condition. The sinh case is fine (sinh: R → R is a bijection between closed intervals), but the tanh case is not covered by A2 as stated.

failure_location.quote: Since $\wDomain = \R^\N$ in both cases, it is easy to check that \ref{as:A2} holds.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Extend Assumption A2 to allow D_rp = closure(ρ_rp(D)) with ρ_rp: D → int(D_rp) invertible (i.e., the image is the interior of a closed interval, with H(z̃) → +∞ as z̃ → ∂D_rp), and adjust the proof of Theorem vector_IRERM (i) to handle the case where h'(z̃) → ∞ at ∂D_rp (giving h'(z̃)^{-1} → 0) rather than the vanishing-derivative condition. Alternatively, establish the tanh case via a limiting argument from compact subdomains [-a,a] → [-tanh(a),tanh(a)] with a → 1⁻.
issues.overall_effect: The entire tanh case (intro theorem part (ii), asymptotic corollary part (ii), non-asymptotic corollary part (ii), and the convergence corollary part (ii)) is not supported by the main theorem's hypotheses as stated. The results are mathematically correct, but the framework's Assumption A2 does not cover the tanh reparametrization without modification.
issues.title: Assumption A2 not satisfied for tanh reparametrization
issues.why_classification: The fix requires a nontrivial adjustment to the main hypothesis (allowing open images with H → ∞ at the boundary) and a corresponding modification to the orthant-preservation proof, but it does not require new proof architecture and all results remain unchanged; it is more than a one-line fix but is contained to the hypothesis and one proof step.
